concepts.label: Active Transaction Record (ATR) - bookkeeping record for an in-flight transaction
concepts.reused_or_minted: reused - this page describes the Java SDK's ATR entries with the identical `_txn:atr-` document-key prefix already documented for SQL++ transactions under this id. Judgment call flagged in cross_component_finding: reused here rather than minting a product-specific sdk:active-transaction-record, on the strength of the identical key-prefix evidence, but this may actually be product-neutral server infrastructure that neither n1ql: nor sdk: should really own.

concepts.reused_or_minted: reused - the SQL++-side config for the same setting this page's Custom Metadata Collections section configures from the SDK side.

concepts.label: SELECT - the SQL++ statement that queries and projects data
concepts.reused_or_minted: reused - named as one of the DML statements permitted within a transaction, and as the target of the KV-to-Query-service operation conversion after the first query statement.

concepts.label: CREATE INDEX - the SQL++ statement that creates a secondary or Composite Vector index
concepts.reused_or_minted: reused - named as an explicit example of a DDL statement NOT supported inside a transaction.

concepts.label: Staged mutation - the transaction mechanic by which a mutated document's post-transaction body is written into the document's XATTRs rather than its main body, invisible until commit and acting as a write-write lock
concepts.reused_or_minted: minted - a genuinely new mechanic concept, distinct from sdk:transaction-attempt-context (the API surface) and from sdk:xattr (the general metadata-field mechanism it is implemented on top of). The page frames this as 'the second mechanic' alongside ATRs as 'the first mechanic', i.e. two named, load-bearing internals of sdk:distributed-transaction.

concepts.label: Extended Attributes (XATTR) - application-specific document metadata
concepts.reused_or_minted: reused - already minted in concept-docs/xattr.json; this page states staged mutations are technically stored in a document's XATTRs.

concepts.label: Custom metadata collection - a non-default collection an application may designate (via TransactionsConfig.metadataCollection / transactionOptions().metadataCollection) to store a transaction's ATR and client-record metadata documents
concepts.reused_or_minted: minted - a genuinely new SDK-side configuration surface, distinct from sdk:transaction-durability/sdk:transaction-timeout (also configured via TransactionsConfig) in that its OBJECT is a keyspace destination for metadata, not a behavioral tuning parameter.

concepts.label: Key-Value Data Operations (get/upsert/insert/replace/remove) via the Collection API

notable_absence.finding: This page describes the identical KV-to-SQL++ operation-conversion mechanism ('subsequent Key-Value operations in the lambda are converted into SQL++ and executed by the Query service') that howtos/distributed-acid-transactions-from-the-sdk.json frames as a PERMISSION-SCOPE change (n1ql:transaction-query-mode, 'the query is executed with the user's query permissions... key-value operations... are also executed with the user's query permissions'). This page frames the SAME mechanism purely as a PERFORMANCE consideration - the entire 'Query Performance Advice' subsection discusses only speed ('likely to be slightly slower') and parallelism, and never once mentions permissions. I deliberately did not force a triggersPermissionModeChange relation here, since the evidence for that specific consequence exists only on the howto page, not this one - two concept-docs pages describing one mechanism through two non-overlapping lenses.

cross_component_finding: This page is the strongest confirmation in the batch that concept-docs/transactions.md REUSES, not reinvents, the promoted transaction vocabulary: sdk:distributed-transaction, sdk:transaction-attempt-context and sdk:transaction-error-handling all appear here in their established senses, just explained mechanistically (ATR entries, staged XATTR mutations, commit/rollback) rather than task-first. The page also surfaces a genuine judgment call: its Active Transaction Records are described with the identical `_txn:atr-` document-key prefix already documented under n1ql:active-transaction-record for SQL++ transactions. I reused that id rather than minting a Java-SDK-specific one, but flag for reconciliation that this may mean the ATR is actually PRODUCT-NEUTRAL server infrastructure that neither the n1ql: nor the sdk: namespace should really own - both surfaces merely read and write the same underlying cluster-level metadata document type.
cross_product_finding: Two dual-surface findings connect this page to the SQL++/Query-service world: (1) n1ql:atrcollection (the SQL++ setting for where ATR/client-record metadata documents live) and this page's TransactionsConfig.metadataCollection()/transactionOptions().metadataCollection() (the SDK setting for the identical purpose) are two API surfaces on the same underlying setting, captured via hasEquivalentEffectAs. (2) This page explicitly tells SDK application writers NOT to drive transactions via the raw SQL++ `BEGIN TRANSACTION` path (n1ql:transactions) even though that Query-service surface exists and is separately documented - both are surfaces onto the same server:distributed-acid-transactions feature, but the SDK page states a clear preference for its own surface over the competing one.
